title: Random Stability of Random Variables
summary: For a random variable $N = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$ we study the following question: When does the sum of $N$ many independent and identically distributed copies of a random variable $X$ have the same law a a nontrivial rescaling of $X$? We show that such $N$-stable random variable exists if and only $1 < \mathbb E[N] < \infty$. Under an additional assumption $\mathbb E[N\ln N] < \infty$, we describe all $N$-stable $X$.
